headline: Growth broadens and profitability swings decisively positive
summary_short: Affirm's quarter ended March 31, 2026 revenue rose 32.6% y/y to $1,039M as GMV grew 35% to $11.6B, while net income swung to $103M from a near-breakeven $2.8M a year ago and diluted EPS reached $0.30.
summary_long: Revenue grew 33% y/y to $1,039M as GMV rose 35% to $11.6B on broad-based growth across merchant network, card network, interest income, and gain on loan sales; active consumers grew 22% to 26.8M. Operating expenses rose a slower 20%, led by processing/servicing (+37%) and provision for credit losses (+33%) tracking loan-book growth, while sales and marketing fell 2% on lower Amazon warrant expense. Operating income swung to $88M from a $8.4M loss a year ago; net income reached $103M (diluted EPS $0.30) versus a near-breakeven $2.8M ($0.01) a year ago. Cash and equivalents rose to $1,723M; long-term debt eased slightly q/q. No forward guidance was stated in the filing.

drivers.explanation: GMV grew 35% on direct-to-consumer growth including Affirm Card and increases in active consumers and transactions per consumer; network revenue, interest income, loan-sale gains, and servicing income all grew double digits.

Revenue grew 33% y/y while credit- and funding-related costs grew slower in aggregate (provision for credit losses +33%, funding costs +6%, loss on loan purchase commitment +19%), expanding gross profit.

Revenue growth of 33% outpaced 20% total operating-expense growth; sales and marketing fell 2% on lower Amazon warrant expense even as provision for credit losses and processing costs grew faster than revenue.
Not explained in the release — EBITDA is not a company-reported measure in this filing; its move is not separately discussed in the MD&A.

Net income swung to $103M from near-breakeven a year ago, driven by the operating income swing to an $88M profit from an $8.4M loss, plus a 38% increase in other income from interest and derivative gains.
Basic weighted-average shares were roughly flat y/y, so basic EPS moved in line with the net income swing from near-breakeven to $103M.
Diluted weighted-average shares grew only about 1% y/y, so diluted EPS moved in line with the net income swing from near-breakeven to $103M.

Cash grew as secured-debt issuance across warehouse and securitization facilities outpaced principal repayments over the fiscal year to date, per the cash-flow statement's financing-activities discussion.
Equity rose primarily on the quarter's $103M net income accreting to retained earnings per the equity roll-forward; no share repurchases were recorded this quarter.
Growth was driven by direct-to-consumer products including Affirm Card and overall increases in active consumers and average transactions per consumer.
Growth was primarily due to a high retention rate of existing consumers and acquisition of new consumers through expansion of active merchants and platform partnerships.

The filing frames results as broad platform growth (GMV +35%, active consumers +22%) alongside continued monitoring of consumer credit and macro/rate uncertainty, with ongoing underwriting adjustments to manage delinquency.
